title.narrative: Output 6.1. Increased capacity of Member States to promote investments in the care economy and a more balanced sharing of family responsibilities

description.narrative: On 29 July 2023, Law 3238-IX on amending the legislation of maternity leave was adopted. This amendment provides women with the opportunity to shift the previously mandatory 70 calendar days of maternity leave from before childbirth to the period after, as long as there are no medical contraindications On 21 February 2023 the ILO provided technical support for the organization of a tripartite strategic consultation for the design of a roadmap to reform the childcare leaves. It gathered 26 participants, including three MPs, Government Commissioner for Gender Policy and her Secretariat, representatives of the Ministry of Economy, Ministry of Education and Science, Ministry of Social Policy, State Statistics Service, Organizations of workers and Employers, UN agencies and several women’s rights NGOs. The agreed roadmap includes actions aiming at modifying the legal framework to comply with the EU Acquis. On October 2023 the ILO assisted in the analysis of the care system in post-Socialist countries that are EU members with the aim to extract lessons learned and good practices for Ukraine.

description.narrative: On July 1, 2022 the information Campaign on undeclared work “Go to Light!” was re-launched following a Presidential statement on the importance of formalisation of labour relations for the war and reconstruction efforts (available on the State Labour Service website). In February, 2022 an overall moratorium on labour inspection visits was introduced after the Russian aggression and labour inspectors focused on providing information to employers and workers about the multiple changes in the legal framework due to the martial law. Between July and December, 2022, the campaign Ukraine works!, about State Labour Service information and consultation services was ongoing, with around 149,000 views of www.pratsia.in.ua. In addition, 365,000 consultations on labour issues, Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) and administrative services through the “Interactive Inspector” service were provided and 57,000 events on technical information and advice were conducted. Furthermore, about 31 million contacts with information materials on undeclared work were registered (through the dissemination of the information in social media, outdoors, through the State Labour Service portal, online webinars, online consultations, information visits to the enterprises etc.). In total 98,298 undeclared workers were regularised following 130,237 State Labour Service (SLS) information visits to employers. Both campaigns were developed with full involvement of the social partners and quarterly monitored in a tripartite manner. On the 22d of December 2022 State Labour Inspectorate approved - in consultations with the social partners - the National action plan for 2023 which includes two key priorities – reduction of undeclared work and improvement of Occupational Safety and Health. The ILO, with support from the European Union, has supported the adaptation of existing information materials of the Go to Light campaign to the war context (video and several infographics). Moreover, the ILO has supported the development of new information materials for the Ukraine works campaign. Furthermore, the ILO has provided training and technical assistance to the State Labour Services to equip them to perform their new tasks, including by providing peer learning with labour inspectors of European Union countries.

Output 6.3. Increased capacity of Member States to develop gender-responsive legislation, policies and measures for a world of work free from violence and harassment

description.narrative: To implement Convention No. 190, in December 2022, after a series of consultations, the Kyiv Regional Trade Unions' Council adopted a Policy on Non-Discrimination, Violence and Harassment in the World of Work in Kyiv region. The policy prohibits all forms of discrimination, violence and harassment at work and establish a workplace mechanism to address such cases at the company level. Following negotiations and consultations, the Policy has been endorsed and signed by the Regional employers' association, and supported by regional authorities. The Policy has a strong HIV component aiming at tackling stigma and discrimination based on real or perceived HIV status as well as scaling up access of working women and men of Kyiv region to voluntary and confidential HIV counselling and testing. For effective policy implementation, an action plan was developed and validated at a trade union Forum conducted in May 2023. To ensure a working environment free from violence and harassment, social partners in the food sector in Kyiv region included provisions on violence and harassment and non-discrimination in their respective collective agreements. To strengthen the capacity of trade unions’ members to effectively implement the Convention and enhance its application in practice, 130 trade union members from different regions of Ukraine, primarily employees of sanatoriums and resorts hosting internally displaced people (IDPs) in western regions, but also trade union leaders from all around Ukraine, received training on psychosocial risks and violence and harassment at work in a war context. As a result of this capacitation training, the Federation of Trade Unions of Ukraine developed proposals on future Recommendations on how collective bargaining agreements should address issues related to gender equality, non-discrimination and violence and harassment. The recommendations are to be considered for adoption at the next meeting of t With the support from UNAIDS Unified Budget, Results and Accountability Framework Country Envelope for Ukraine, the ILO provided training on violence and harassment at work for 40 trade union leaders in different sectors of Kyiv region who, in their turn, organized a peer learning for at least 60 more working women and men. ILO also provided technical support to the development of the draft Policy on Non-Discrimination, Violence and Harassment in the World of Work in Kyiv region.
